entries.name: Moses Watkins — Free First Registration
entries.hint: A Port Gellhorn mechanic will put your first stolen car in your name for nothing — choose wisely.
entries.spoiler_details: In Chapter 2, after the Girls' Trip mission, Vicki sends Lucia to Moses Watkins at Watkins Auto Parts in Port Gellhorn. Moses teaches the WAiNK scanning app and the Slim Jim, and offers to register Lucia's first car completely free — a one-time deal, since later registrations cost several times a car's sale value. He only accepts cars with no tracker, and refuses large utility vehicles and cars stolen right next to his shop. Decline his first offer, fetch something worth keeping, respray it, and register it; it then becomes a personal vehicle you can summon with the Scooter Bros app.

entries.spoiler_details: Head to Fontana Motorsports in Capri, just off the highway exit, in daytime after about 10 AM. Skip the Pfister Comets and Pegassi Toros lined up out front — they all carry trackers Moses won't accept. At the back-right corner of the lot sits a beat-up Invetero Coquette '64 with no alarm and no tracker. It normally costs $29,150 to register, making it one of the biggest savings for Moses' free first registration; alternatively Moses pays about $6,600 for it. Downside: it has no trunk, so no room for contraband stashes or outfits.

entries.name: Maibatsu Penumbra FF '97 (Paul Walker Tribute)
entries.hint: A bright green movie-famous coupe sleeps in a villa garage on an island between the city and the beach.
entries.spoiler_details: On Vespucci Island, one of the Rialto Islands between Vice City and Vice Beach, find the villa near the middle of the island with a white gate facing its garage (one guide places the house on Neptune Circle, behind a tall hedge). Break into the garage and switch off the alarm on the wall left of the entrance, then open the door: inside is the green 1997 Maibatsu Penumbra FF with blue graphics and the plate 'HAD YOU', a tribute to Paul Walker's Eclipse from The Fast and the Furious. Entry is by smashing a window and hotwiring, or quieter with the Slim Jim (Chapter 2) or Snap Gun (Chapter 3). It has no tracker and comes pre-fitted with upgrades (acceleration rated 7.6/10), with 2 storage slots. Warning: registering any stolen car with Moses requires a respray, which strips this car's unique movie livery, so decide whether you want it as a keeper or as a collector's piece first. Registration is $6,750 if you miss the free slot — and it must be registered with Moses early on; Pay 'n' Spray registration only opens in Chapter 3 (one guide's 'register at a Pay 'n' Spray' line is wrong for the early game).

entries.spoiler_details: Randy, a fence based at the Leonida Auto World dealership in Balcero (his garage shows as a green RK icon), opens his Wish List in Chapter 3 after the mission Clonin' Keys, Makin' GS, which also gives you the Key Cloner app for keyless high-end cars. He pays about $30,000 per car, rising to $35,000 or more in perfect condition, and finishing the list unlocks the Supply & Demand trophy. Most list cars carry trackers: a standard (yellow) one alerts police if you stop too long, while an advanced (red) one reports you whenever you drive too slowly, so plan the route to his garage before you steal.

entries.name: Refuelling & Gas Stations (57)
entries.hint: Yes, cars need fuel — no, it is not the chore the pre-launch rumours promised.
entries.spoiler_details: Vehicles do burn fuel, and a dry tank stops the car — but tanks last a long time, and PC Gamer's hands-on verdict is that the pump's Repair option matters more in practice than fuel. There are 57 gas stations (Vice-Dale 26, Kelly 12, Mariana 7, Leonard 6, Lummox 6). Park at a pump, choose Services → Refuel, and hold R2/RT (one hands-on example: ~$40). D-pad Down shows the fuel gauge: green plenty, yellow low, red nearly empty. EVs charge instead of refuelling. The Services button itself is reported as Cross/A by Space4Games and GameRant but Triangle on PS5 by Shacknews — follow the on-screen prompt.

entries.name: Wanted Level & the Heat System
entries.hint: Six stars, and the police remember what you look like — losing sight is not losing heat.
entries.spoiler_details: Wanted runs to six stars, and a crime must be witnessed or trigger an alarm/CCTV before police respond at all. Star states: hollow = reported but suspect unknown; solid white = seen; flashing = visual lost; solid red = pursuit lost but the Heat area is still combed. Six Heat recognition icons sit under the stars — face, outfit, vehicle, weapon, partner, CCTV — and each clears separately; breaking line of sight alone does not clear your description. Police do not appear on the radar.
